name: Hadal-Moulin
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by ancient meteor crater, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.
The silence has texture, close to audible. Old survey teams left notes about hearing their own heartbeats as knocking. Ambush predators lie beneath the thermally warm silt, patient as geology.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
There is money in water, dark crystals, carbon and helium-3 and history in the rocks, and the two keep interfering with each other. Mediators do brisk business at inflated rates.
